look_here_first: Start with the stem: giant goldenrod has a mostly smooth/glabrous lower stem, long narrow 3-nerved leaves, creeping rhizomes, and a broad arching panicle of many small yellow heads.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — project Hays-local source pool. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center herbarium index includes Solidago gigantea. Williamson — dedicated county flora documents S. gigantea.

best_field_traits: lower stem glabrous to nearly glabrous
often moist riparian or mesic sites
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with S. altissima, the lower stem is much smoother and less hairy. Compared with S. juliae, S. gigantea is more strongly rhizomatous and typically has smoother stems with narrower leaves.
